concept.name: HTTP Semantics & Caching

relationships.description: Connects HTTP Semantics & Caching to api gateway in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: HTTP caching (RFC 9111) uses explicit freshness lifetimes, validation headers (ETag/Last-Modified), and Vary keys so browsers, CDNs, and reverse proxies serve safe, fast responses without stale leaks.
spark.keyTakeaway: Separate immutable static assets (Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable) from dynamic APIs (Cache-Control: no-cache + ETag revalidation), and use Vary carefully so you never fragment cache hit ratios or leak user-specific responses.

concept.whyItMatters: Every uncached request that hits an origin server pays full TLS/origin compute, database I/O, and cross-region RTT (50–250 ms). Properly configured HTTP caching offloads 70–95% of traffic to edge CDNs (Cloudflare, Fastly, CloudFront) and browser caches, cutting p95 latency under 15 ms. Conversely, a single misconfigured Cache-Control or missing Vary header can cache authenticated PII on a shared CDN and serve User A's account page to User B.
whenToUse: Content-hashed static assets (JS, CSS, fonts, images) where filenames change on every build, enabling 1-year immutable caching.
Public or semi-static read APIs (catalogs, feature flags, product pages) where 10–60 second edge TTLs plus stale-while-revalidate absorb traffic spikes.
Large payloads (JSON schemas, media manifests) where ETag / If-None-Match conditional requests turn 500 KB downloads into 300-byte 304 Not Modified responses.
whenNotToUse: Personalized, authenticated, or financial endpoints unless explicitly marked Cache-Control: private, no-store (or private, max-age=0, must-revalidate).
Real-time transactional state (live inventory counts, payment status) where even a 2-second stale read breaks business invariants.
Non-idempotent or state-mutating methods (POST, PUT, DELETE), which RFC 9111 forbids standard caches from serving without explicit invalidation.
keyPoints: Cache-Control directives govern storage and freshness: `no-store` forbids all caching; `no-cache` allows storage but mandates origin revalidation before every reuse; `private` restricts storage to the browser, blocking shared CDNs.

Freshness lifetime is computed from `s-maxage` (shared caches only) -> `max-age` -> `Expires`, compared against the response `Age` header; `stale-while-revalidate` lets caches serve slightly expired content while refreshing asynchronously.
Conditional validation uses strong/weak `ETag` (`If-None-Match`) or `Last-Modified` (`If-Modified-Since`) to return `304 Not Modified` without resending the response body.

The `Vary` header defines secondary cache keys (e.g., `Vary: Accept-Encoding, Accept-Language`); `Vary: User-Agent` or `Vary: Cookie` destroys CDN cache hit ratios by creating thousands of distinct keys.

Unsafe methods (`POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`) must invalidate matching cached URI entries on compliant caches, while `GET` and `HEAD` are safe and cacheable by default when freshness headers are present.

examples.title: Immutable Asset Hashing + Stale-While-Revalidate on a Retail Storefront
examples.scenario: A storefront serves `app.8f3c2a.js` (420 KB) and `/api/v1/catalog/featured` (65 KB JSON, updated every 5 minutes) behind Fastly.
examples.outcome: Static bundles carry `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, yielding a 99.4% browser/CDN hit rate and zero 304 round-trips. The catalog endpoint returns `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300` with a strong `ETag`, keeping edge p99 latency at 12 ms while masking origin 502 blips.

examples.title: Preventing Cross-User Cache Poisoning on an Authenticated BFF
examples.scenario: An engineering team places Cloudflare in front of `/api/me/profile`, which authenticates via a session cookie and omits `Cache-Control`. A misconfigured CDN page rule caches all 200 OK responses for 5 minutes.
examples.outcome: By enforcing `Cache-Control: private, no-store` on all authenticated routes and `Vary: Authorization` where token-scoped responses are edge-cached, the team eliminates PII leakage while keeping public `/pricing` pages cached at 96% hit ratio.

tradeOffs.factor: Long TTLs vs. Instant Content Updates
tradeOffs.pro: Maximizes edge offload (95%+) and shields origins from thundering herds.
tradeOffs.con: Requires content-hashed filenames or active purge APIs (e.g., Cloudflare/Fastly surrogate-key purges) to retract bad deploys.

tradeOffs.pro: `no-cache` with `ETag` saves bandwidth via `304 Not Modified` while guaranteeing freshness on every request.
tradeOffs.con: Still incurs a full network round-trip to the origin (or shielding POP) to validate the ETag on every load.

tradeOffs.factor: Granular Vary Headers vs. Cache Hit Ratio
tradeOffs.pro: Prevents serving compressed gzip bytes to non-gzip clients or wrong-language pages.
tradeOffs.con: Every unique value combination of `Vary` headers multiplies cache keys; `Vary: *` or `Vary: User-Agent` collapses hit rates toward 0%.

failureModes.name: Authenticated PII Cache Leak
failureModes.description: An endpoint returns user-specific data with `Cache-Control: public` or no `Cache-Control` header behind a permissive CDN rule, causing the shared cache to serve one user's data to subsequent visitors.
failureModes.mitigation: Default all authenticated API middleware to `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and add automated CI/gateway assertions that block `public` or `s-maxage` when `Set-Cookie` or `Authorization` is present.

failureModes.name: Cache Key Explosion via Unbounded Vary
failureModes.description: Returning `Vary: User-Agent` or `Vary: Accept-Encoding, Accept` splits a single popular URL into tens of thousands of cache variants across Chrome/Safari/Firefox minor versions.
failureModes.mitigation: Normalize `Accept-Encoding` at the CDN edge to `{gzip, br, identity}` and strip `Vary: User-Agent` in favor of responsive CSS or normalized device-class headers.

failureModes.name: Thundering Herd on Synchronized TTL Expiry
failureModes.description: A hot endpoint with `s-maxage=60` expires simultaneously across 50 edge POPs, sending 50x–500x concurrent origin requests that overwhelm database connections.
failureModes.mitigation: Combine `s-maxage=60` with `stale-while-revalidate=120` and `stale-if-error=600`, plus request coalescing (collapsed forwarding) at the reverse proxy/CDN.

failureModes.name: Misunderstanding no-cache vs. no-store
failureModes.description: Developers set `Cache-Control: no-cache` expecting sensitive medical or financial payloads never to be written to disk, unaware that browsers still store the response locally and merely revalidate it.
failureModes.mitigation: Use `Cache-Control: no-store` for sensitive data that must never touch disk or shared memory, and reserve `no-cache` for payloads that should be cached but revalidated.

commonMistakes: Confusing `no-cache` (store, but revalidate before reuse) with `no-store` (do not store anywhere).
Omitting `immutable` on fingerprinted static assets, causing browsers on manual reload (F5) to fire unnecessary `If-None-Match` revalidation bursts.
Setting both `Expires` and `Cache-Control` with conflicting values, forgetting that `Cache-Control: max-age` / `s-maxage` always overrides `Expires` per RFC 9111.
Returning weak ETags (`W/"abc"`) for byte-range requests (`Range: bytes=0-1023`), which RFC 9110 forbids for `206 Partial Content` coalescing.
Using `Vary: Cookie` on public marketing pages because an analytics cookie is present, reducing CDN cache hit rate to near zero.

sections.content:
## The idea

HTTP is not merely a transport framing protocol—**RFC 9110** (Semantics) and **RFC 9111** (Caching) encode a distributed caching contract directly into request and response headers. Every intermediary—browser cache, corporate proxy, Varnish/Nginx reverse proxy, and global CDN—reads the same headers to answer two questions: *Can I store this response?* and *Can I reuse it without asking the origin?*

**Storage rules** come from `Cache-Control`: `no-store` forbids persistence; `private` allows only single-user browser caches; `public` permits shared caches. **Freshness rules** compare a response's calculated lifetime (`s-maxage` for shared caches, else `max-age`, else `Expires - Date`) against its `Age`. While `Age < lifetime`, the response is *fresh* and served directly from cache in 1–15 ms.

Once `Age >= lifetime` (or if `no-cache` was specified), the entry becomes *stale*. Rather than discarding it, the cache sends a **conditional request** (`If-None-Match: "v42"` or `If-Modified-Since`) to the origin. If the resource has not changed, the origin replies `304 Not Modified` with an empty body and refreshed headers, resetting freshness without transferring megabytes of payload.

## Concrete walkthrough

Trace a product catalog request `GET /v1/products/42` with `Accept-Encoding: br` traversing a Browser -> Cloudflare Edge POP -> Origin API (Node/Go + Postgres):

1. **Cold Cache Miss (`t = 0s`)**: The browser has no entry. Cloudflare hashes the primary key `(GET, https://api.example.com/v1/products/42)` and misses. It forwards the request to Origin. Origin queries Postgres (18 ms) and responds `200 OK` with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=15, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=120`, `ETag: "9d4f2a"`, and `Vary: Accept-Encoding`.
2. **Shared & Private Storage**: Cloudflare stores the Brotli-compressed body keyed by `(URL, Accept-Encoding=br)` with a 60-second shared TTL. The browser stores it for 15 seconds (`max-age=15`).
3. **Fresh Edge Hit (`t = 25s`)**: A second user in the same city requests `/v1/products/42`. Cloudflare sees `Age: 25 < s-maxage: 60` and returns `200 OK` in 9 ms—Origin sees zero traffic.
4. **Stale-While-Revalidate (`t = 75s`)**: Another user arrives at `t = 75s`. The 60s `s-maxage` has expired, but `75s < 60s + 120s` (`stale-while-revalidate`). Cloudflare immediately serves the stale cached response in 9 ms while asynchronously sending `GET /v1/products/42` with `If-None-Match: "9d4f2a"` to Origin.
5. **304 Revalidation**: Origin checks the row version, sees it is still `"9d4f2a"`, and returns `304 Not Modified` (no body, 220 bytes of headers). Cloudflare resets `Age: 0` for another 60 seconds.

sections.eyebrow: 03 / Cache keys, Vary, and surrogate keys
sections.content:
## Cache keys, Vary, and surrogate keys

By default, an HTTP cache keys entries by `(HTTP Method, Scheme, Host, Path + Query)`. Two subtle mechanisms control key cardinality and invalidation:

- **`Vary` (Secondary Cache Keys)**: When an origin returns `Vary: Accept-Encoding, Accept-Language`, the cache stores separate variants per header value tuple. Avoid `Vary: User-Agent` or `Vary: Cookie`—a single popular endpoint can fracture into 50,000+ cold keys. If you must vary on auth or device type, normalize at the edge into a coarse header (e.g., `X-Device-Class: mobile|desktop`).
- **`Surrogate-Key` / `Cache-Tag`**: URL-based purging fails when a single product update affects `/products/42`, `/category/shoes`, and `/search?q=running`. CDNs like Fastly and Cloudflare support `Surrogate-Key: product-42 cat-shoes` (stripped before reaching the browser), enabling O(1) tag-based invalidation across thousands of cached URLs simultaneously while keeping `s-maxage` high (e.g., 24 hours).

## Cache-Control directive reference

| Directive | Browser Storage | Shared CDN Storage | Revalidation Behavior | Typical Use Case |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` | Yes (1 year) | Yes (1 year) | None, even on reload | Content-hashed JS/CSS/fonts (`app.8f3c2a.js`) |
| `public, s-maxage=60, max-age=10` | Yes (10s) | Yes (60s) | Revalidates after respective TTL | Public APIs where edge can be warmer than browser |
| `no-cache` | Yes | Yes (if `public`) | Must revalidate (`304`) before every use | HTML shells (`index.html`) pointing to hashed assets |
| `private, no-store` | No | No | Never stored; full fetch every time | Banking, PII, `/api/me`, auth tokens |
| `stale-while-revalidate=120` | Yes | Yes | Serves stale during window, refreshes async | Catalogs, feeds, CMS pages tolerating brief staleness |

## Failure modes

- **Web cache poisoning via unkeyed headers**: If an origin reads `X-Forwarded-Host` or `X-Original-URL` to build script URLs in HTML without listing that header in `Vary`, an attacker can send a crafted header on a cache miss and poison the CDN entry for all subsequent users.
- **Cache stampede on TTL expiration**: Without `stale-while-revalidate` or request coalescing (collapsed forwarding), a hot key expiring at `s-maxage=60` unleashes hundreds of simultaneous origin queries.
- **Set-Cookie stripping or accidental caching**: Sending `Set-Cookie` on a `200 OK` with `Cache-Control: public` can either cache a session cookie for all users or cause CDNs to silently bypass caching.
- **Query string cache busting abuse**: Attackers appending `?cb=random123` to bypass CDN caches and hit the origin directly unless query parameters are allowlisted in the CDN cache key.

## Designing cacheable APIs & HTML shells

A reliable web architecture pairs **two distinct caching tiers**:

1. **HTML Entrypoints (`index.html`)**: Serve with `Cache-Control: no-cache` (or `s-maxage=10, stale-while-revalidate=60`) and a strong `ETag`. Clients always get the latest deployment manifest via a fast `304` check.
2. **Fingerprinted Assets & Read APIs**: Serve JS/CSS/images with content hashes and `max-age=31536000, immutable`. For read APIs, strip cookies on public endpoints, prefer `Surrogate-Key` invalidation over tiny TTLs, and set `stale-if-error=86400` so the CDN continues serving the last good response if the origin returns `500`/`502`/`504`.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Default all authenticated or user-scoped endpoints to `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.
- [ ] Use `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` for all content-hashed static bundles.
- [ ] Add `stale-while-revalidate` and `stale-if-error` on public read APIs to eliminate stampedes and mask origin blips.
- [ ] Audit `Vary` headers; never emit `Vary: User-Agent` or `Vary: *` on CDN-fronted routes.
- [ ] Enable request coalescing (collapsed forwarding) at the reverse proxy/CDN for cache misses.
- [ ] Ensure `Surrogate-Key` / `Cache-Tag` headers are stripped at the edge before forwarding responses to browsers.

interviewProblems.title: HTTP Semantics & Caching
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on HTTP Semantics & Caching. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: HTTP caching (RFC 9111) uses explicit freshness lifetimes, validation headers (ETag/Last-Modified), and Vary keys so browsers, CDNs, and reverse proxies serve safe, fast responses without stale leaks.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Edge CDN / Varnish applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Origin API.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Origin API experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Default all authenticated API middleware to `Cache-Control: private, no-store` and add automated CI/gateway assertions that block `public` or `s-maxage` when `Set-Cookie` or `Authorization` is present.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Separate immutable static assets (Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable) from dynamic APIs (Cache-Control: no-cache + ETag revalidation), and use Vary carefully so you never fragment cache hit ratios or leak user-specific responses.
Avoid trap: Confusing `no-cache` (store, but revalidate before reuse) with `no-store` (do not store anywhere).
Avoid trap: Omitting `immutable` on fingerprinted static assets, causing browsers on manual reload (F5) to fire unnecessary `If-None-Match` revalidation bursts.
When to reach for it: Content-hashed static assets (JS, CSS, fonts, images) where filenames change on every build, enabling 1-year immutable caching.
When to reach for it: Public or semi-static read APIs (catalogs, feature flags, product pages) where 10–60 second edge TTLs plus stale-while-revalidate absorb traffic spikes.

putItTogether.title: Putting Http Semantics Caching Together
putItTogether.summary: Separate immutable static assets (Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable) from dynamic APIs (Cache-Control: no-cache + ETag revalidation), and use Vary carefully so you never fragment cache hit ratios or leak user-specific responses.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Http Semantics Caching before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Static bundles carry `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, yielding a 99.4% browser/CDN hit rate and zero 304 round-trips. The catalog endpoint returns `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=300` with a strong `ETag`, keeping edge p99 latency at 12 ms while masking origin 502 blips.
